channel.title: Hui Ning · Blog
channel.description: Thoughts on life, attention, AI, and biological design.

item.title: One life. What follows?
item.description: A finite life changes how I weigh direction, action, and other people’s opinions.

item.title: Choosing where my attention goes
item.description: There is a great deal worth reading. I want enough time to work out which questions deserve my thought.

item.title: Leaving context for my future self
item.description: After sleep, I may remember a conclusion without being able to recover the reasoning. I want to leave enough context to continue.

item.title: Forming a judgment I can stand behind
item.description: I want more perspectives, and I want to know which reasons are strong enough to change my mind.

item.title: How I get agents to finish the work
item.description: Define the result, sustain the work, and let independent reviewers inspect what was actually produced.

item.title: AI4Bio: What evidence comes after a prediction?
item.description: I want to understand why scaling helps, whether predictions hold across conditions, and which research decisions models can improve.

item.title: AI as intellectual leverage
item.description: AI changes what I think one person can attempt. It also makes understanding the problem and judging the result more important.

item.title: Turning understanding into action
item.description: Working with AI makes me examine my own work: the goal, what action reveals, and whether the next decision changes.

item.title: When should a biological system act?
item.description: My doctoral questions about sensing cell state lead to an interest in when biological functions start, how long they last, and how they end.
